hypothesis: Gravity tilt-angle edge corridors target steep buried normal faults that lack a preserved topographic scarp and are therefore absent from the USGS/INGENIOUS scarp catalogue. Tilt angle = atan2(|dg/dz|, |grad_h g|) is ~90 deg over steep vertical contacts (faults) and ~0 deg over flat bedding; weighting horizontal-gradient magnitude by cos(tilt)^2 selects steep-contact edges of any strike. Named non-fault mimic: equant plutonic intrusions and circular density anomalies produce horizontal-gradient magnitude but low tilt steepness, down-weighted by cos(tilt)^2.
mechanism: B11 (vertical gravity derivative), B13 (isostatic gravity anomaly, differentiated for N-S derivative), B18 (E-W gravity horizontal derivative). hgm = sqrt(hg_ew^2 + hg_ns^2); tilt = atan2(|vg|, hgm); S_raw = hgm * cos(tilt)^2; S = percentile rank over valid footprint. Catalogue used only for masking: dots off-catalogue and >2 px from it.
non_fault_mimic: Equant plutonic intrusions, circular playa/evaporite density bodies, and diffuse basement-terrane boundaries produce gravity gradient magnitude but not steep (near-90 deg) tilt angles; cos(tilt)^2 down-weights them.
difference_from_existing_lanes: No lane computes a gravity tilt angle. GRAVQUAD uses analytic-signal amplitude x structure-tensor coherence (dip-blind, responds to any elongated gradient blob). COULOMB-LOQO assumes fixed N15E conjugate shear planes inside a supervised classifier. CURIE-DEMAG uses RTP variance suppression x MT clay-cap flank x demag bowl. TILTANGLE explicitly selects steep near-vertical contacts.
